first_impression.reaction: Emily sent it, so I read it. It's mostly about the website side, which is her department, not mine. But the opening line about 'your aunt in Perth' made me think straight away of my sister and Mum, who will never fill in a form on a phone. I kept going to see whether it said anything about them, and about who is actually looking after the money and the guests.

journey.quote: It is where your aunt in Perth, your school friends in London and your colleague in Singapore all tell you the same things: whether they are coming, which nights they will be there, what they eat and when their flight lands.
journey.reaction: Plain and sensible. It's written for grown-ups, not influencers. Good start.

journey.section: The five kinds of wedding RSVP website compared
journey.quote: Planning app with RSVP | Couples who want replies to feed the seating plan | How replies flow to the seating chart and guest list | Another app to learn
journey.reaction: The table is clear enough, but this is Emily's job. I skimmed it. I'm glad it is honest that each option has a downside.

journey.section: What changes between paid tiers and those at no cost
journey.quote: If the answers that matter sit behind a paid tier, upgrade early rather than rebuild halfway through.
journey.reaction: Sensible advice about money. Pay once, properly, rather than twice. I'd tell her the same.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, so these answers have somewhere useful to go.
journey.reaction: This is the sentence that matters to me. Payments, with a person. I'd want to know a lot more about how deposits are handled, but at least someone is named as responsible.

journey.section: Meal and dietary needs per person
journey.quote: Keep the question to what the caterer needs to cook safely, for example, "Any allergies or dietary needs we should share with the chef?"
journey.reaction: Good, they think about allergies. But there is nothing anywhere about mobility or access needs. My mother uses a walking frame. That's the question I'd want on the form, and it isn't there.

journey.section: Guest privacy and who can see the site
journey.quote: Whatever the law asks, good manners ask more: password-protect the site, share the list only with the suppliers who need it, and delete what you no longer need after the wedding.
journey.reaction: I like this. Careful, not flippant about people's details. It reads like someone has actually checked the rules.

journey.section: QR code RSVPs and when to print the link too
journey.quote: So print the RSVP web address beside the code, short and easy to type, for guests who would rather not scan.
journey.reaction: Thank you. Half my side of the family won't scan anything. Nice not to be treated as old-fashioned for that.

journey.quote: Yes. Offer a phone number or email for guests who would rather reply another way, and add their answers yourself.
journey.reaction: Right answer, but it's tucked at the very bottom. This is the bit I'd forward to my husband, and I had to hunt for it. It could say plainly that it's often the older relatives.

journey.section: Plan the weekend, not just the replies
journey.quote: Turning them into a weekend where every guest is looked after is where a Wedded Advisor comes in: one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact.
journey.reaction: One named person is exactly what I want. I'd still want to speak to them on the phone before anything is booked, and the page doesn't tell me how that works.

unanswered_questions: If we use a Wedded Advisor, who do I ring if something goes wrong in the middle of the night, overseas time?
How are deposits paid to overseas suppliers, and is our money protected?
Are quotes and fees given in AUD and agreed in writing?
Can I speak to someone by phone before we commit to anything?
Will anyone help with older guests' mobility, transfers and travel insurance?
would_share_with: My husband, mainly for the bit about a single point of contact and the privacy section
My sister, for the part about printing the web address beside the QR code

cta_reaction.quote: Start the conversation with our Wedded Concierge team.
cta_reaction.why: I'd click to find out whether I can get a person on the phone, but this page is about websites, not about the money. I'd let Emily click first and then ask my own questions about deposits and contracts.

top_3_changes: Add an access question to the RSVP list so older guests are planned for. Old: "- Arrival and departure dates, and where they are staying" New: "- Arrival and departure dates, and where they are staying\n- Any mobility or access needs we should plan for"

Make the offline reply option speak to older relatives. Old: "Yes. Offer a phone number or email for guests who would rather reply another way, and add their answers yourself." New: "Yes. For older relatives or anyone who would rather not use a website, offer a phone number or email and add their answers yourself."

Repeat in the closing what the Wedded Advisor is responsible for (already stated earlier in the post). Old: "one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact." New: "one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact who plans venue, travel, vendors and payments with you."

open_questions.question: My main questions (deposit protection, AUD quotes, phone contact out of hours) are outside this post's deliberate scope. Should they be routed to a separate piece rather than this draft?
